summary: The study investigates the impact of O3 feeding time on the physical and electrical properties of TiO2 films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) for memory capacitor applications. The films were deposited on Ru electrodes at 250 °C using TTIP as the titanium precursor and O3 as the oxidant. The results show that while the density, composition, chemical state, and crystalline structure of the TiO2 films remained largely unaffected by O3 feeding time, increasing the O3 feeding time beyond 3 s led to surface roughening and severe local protrusions, which significantly increased leakage current density. A minimum tox of 0.8 nm with a leakage current density of 1×10−7 A/cm2 at 0.8 V was achieved at an O3 feeding time of 2–3 s.
evidence: The effect of the O3 feeding time on the physical and electrical properties of TiO2 thin films on Ru electrodes was investigated. The density, composition, chemical state, and crystalline structure of the TiO2 films were almost identical, irrespective of the O3 feeding time, even when the TiO2 films were grown under subsaturated conditions with respect to the O3 feeding. However, increasing the O3 feeding time to more than 3 s brought about surface roughening and severe local protrusion of the films, which significantly increased their leakage current density. The conduction band offset of the film surface was generally small and was not increased by increasing the O3 feeding time nor was the leakage current improved. Consequently, a minimum tox of 0.8 nm with a leakage current density /H11021/H110111 /H1100310−7 A/c m2 at an applied voltage of 0.8 V was achieved at an O3 feeding time of 2–3 s.
